nodes.label: Client-Side Aggregation Anti-Pattern
nodes.rationale: Every page is a client component that pulls the full dataset then aggregates in the browser. Cost therefore scales with viewer count, not data size: 50 users each recompute the identical Kementerian-wide totals from scratch.

nodes.label: Ringkasan Page Load Budget
nodes.rationale: One /ringkasan visit measured at ~21,700 rows over ~26 sequential requests and ~19.7 MB of raw JSON, to render ~40 aggregate numbers and 10 charts.

nodes.label: Connection Pool Saturation at 50 Users
nodes.rationale: ~1,300 concurrent requests against a ~10-15 connection pool queue then time out; users press Refresh, adding 26 more requests each, so the failure mode is a snowball rather than gradual slowdown.

nodes.label: kd_rup Type Mismatch Across Tables
nodes.rationale: kd_rup is a number in api_paket_penyedia_terumumkan, ai_kurasi_paket and paket_anggaran_penyedia but text in paket_e_purchasing, non_tender_selesai, pencatatan_non_tender_realisasi, tender_selesai_nilai and risiko_pengadaan. Every join must cast, which disables ordinary indexes and forces reliance on exact-match expression indexes.

nodes.label: Brittle Expression Index Dependency
nodes.rationale: Expression indexes only serve a query when the expression matches character for character. Changing a JOIN to wrap LTRIM already silently orphaned the old index once and produced statement timeouts, so the current setup is a tambalan that any future edit can break.

nodes.label: Unindexable split_part Join on kd_rup
nodes.rationale: The pengadaan-langsung branch joins on split_part(kd_rup, ';', 1) because kd_rup can hold two concatenated codes. No expression index covers it, so that 6,023-row branch is always fully scanned — which is why offset 0 and offset 7000 measured the same latency.

nodes.label: Money Columns Stored as Text
nodes.rationale: nilai_realisasi, pagu, nilai_kontrak and related columns are text, so views run REPLACE plus two CASTs per row inside SUM(). Beyond the cost, a single malformed row makes the whole dashboard query fail rather than merely report a wrong number.

nodes.label: Unfiltered tahun_anggaran Growth
nodes.rationale: Every ingest table carries tahun_anggaran but no client fetch filters on it, so the payload grows each fiscal year independently of user count — a slowdown that arrives on a calendar, not on traffic.

nodes.label: Unordered .range() Pagination
nodes.rationale: All nine paginated fetch loops call .range() without .order(). A UNION ALL has no ordering guarantee, so pages can duplicate or skip rows — most likely under load — producing silently wrong totals with no error surfaced.

nodes.label: Materialized View as Primary Remedy
nodes.rationale: Pre-computing the gabungan view once per SIRUP ingest moves the casts, split_part join and correlated subqueries off the request path. Ranked first because an RPC built over the live view would still pay full materialisation cost per call.

nodes.label: Server-Side Cache Layer
nodes.rationale: Caching the aggregate on the server severs the link between viewer count and database load: 1, 50 or 200 users cost one query per revalidation window. This is the step that actually answers the 50-user question.

nodes.label: Export Libraries in Critical Path
nodes.rationale: exceljs, jspdf and html-to-image are statically imported into the Ringkasan client chunk, so every visitor downloads ~1.4 MB for features most never trigger. Deferring them to click time cuts initial JS to roughly 350 KB.

nodes.label: components_json Payload Dominance
nodes.rationale: RisikoInsightPanel pulls components_json for 7,741 rows — 15 MB, about 79% of the whole page budget — to draw two charts that need roughly 30 grouped counts.

nodes.label: Anon-Readable Procurement Data
nodes.rationale: Full paket and risiko rows were readable with only the browser-embedded anon key and no session. PPK scoping is enforced at the view layer, so restricted rows still reach the client before being hidden.

nodes.label: Eight-Step Remediation Plan
nodes.rationale: Ordered by impact per hour: materialised view, year filter, aggregate RPC, cache, risiko rollup, ordered pagination, deferred export bundle, then schema normalisation as the only permanent cure.

nodes.label: Dependency-Ordered Migration Phases
nodes.rationale: Objects are rebuilt in dependency order (extensions, tables, CSV import, foundation views, base master-data views, dashboard views, gabungan, indexes) rather than historical commit order, because several views are redefined across multiple files.

nodes.label: Superseded SQL File List
nodes.rationale: Eleven older SQL files are explicitly marked do-not-run on a fresh database because later patches overwrote them; some also contain INSERTs that fail against an empty schema.

nodes.label: Tables Born From CSV Import
nodes.rationale: api_paket_penyedia_terumumkan and api_paket_swakelola_terumumkan have no DDL at all — they are created by Supabase Table Editor CSV import, so their column types come from import-time inference rather than a declared schema.

nodes.label: Object to Final-File Map
nodes.rationale: Quick-reference table naming which file holds the authoritative definition of each view, since a view's final shape is reached cumulatively across several patch files.

nodes.label: Numbered Turnkey Migration Sequence
nodes.rationale: A numbered subset (00 to 64) of the final SQL scripts that can be run straight through without consulting the runbook; the legacy sql/ files are left untouched as history.

nodes.label: Cumulative View Patching (40-44)
nodes.rationale: Each patch touches several views at once, so each view only reaches its final form after 40 through 44 run in order. Kept deliberately rather than rewriting the definitions, to reproduce the deployed state with less risk of divergence.

nodes.label: Manual CSV Import Checkpoint
nodes.rationale: Step 25 is a comment-only checklist, not a runnable script: the operator must stop and perform the CSV imports by hand before continuing to the view and index files.
